children: Viking Global Technologies reported two financing actions. The company amended its $1.2 million convertible note with FK Venture, extending maturity to the earlier of April 1, 2027 or a triggering senior lender default, and resetting the conversion price to $0.15 per share or $0.02 upon a senior note default. Separately, subsidiary Viking Protection Systems arranged a $300,000 short-term loan with accredited investors, featuring a fixed 10% interest amount and a personal guaranty from CEO James A. Doris. The moves aim to bolster liquidity and provide flexibility while addressing potential senior lender default dynamics.
Agreement 1: Viking Global Technologies Extends $1.2M FK Convertible Note to Apr 2027, Resets Conversion Price
: Amendment to unsecured convertible promissory note
: Until earlier of Apr 1 2027 or senior note default
: Extend maturity and adjust conversion terms amid senior lender risk
Agreement 2: Viking Protection Systems Raises $300,000 Via Short-Term Note Backed by CEO Guaranty
: Short-term promissory note with fixed interest and personal guaranty
: Earlier of Dec 31 2026 or VPS financing close
